title: SEO
description: Search visibility isn't a switch you flip once. Here's what actually moves the needle, engine by engine.

entries.question: What is SEO?
entries.answer:
SEO stands for Search Engine Optimization - the practice of shaping a website so search engines can find it, understand it, and rank it favorably for the terms people actually search. In practice that covers three things: technical health (page speed, mobile-friendliness, whether the site can be crawled at all), content quality (does the page genuinely answer the query), and authority signals (links and mentions from other trustworthy sites).

It isn't a project with a finish line - it's a maintenance discipline. Rankings shift as competitors publish new content, as algorithms update, and as a site ages without attention, so what ranks well today has to be revisited as the landscape changes.

It's also not one unified target. Optimization is search-engine specific - Google, Bing, and platform-native search tools (like the one built into GoDaddy's website builder) each run their own ranking logic, crawl behavior, and quality signals. A page tuned only for Google's preferences can under-perform elsewhere. The general rule holds across all of them, though: the higher your optimization score against a given engine's rules, the more likely your site is to surface in that engine's results.

title: Mobile vs. Desktop
description: How visitors actually reach your site, and why designing for the smaller screen first isn't optional anymore.

entries.question: How much of my traffic is coming from mobile?
entries.answer:
Mobile devices account for roughly 65% of all web traffic, and that share continues to grow. For most client sites, that means the majority of first impressions happen on a phone screen, not a desktop monitor.

That has real design consequences: navigation, load speed, tap targets, and layout all need to be built mobile-first, with desktop treated as the expanded view rather than the default. A site that only looks polished on a wide monitor is optimizing for the minority of its own visitors.
